title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA0LE_0LC1LC_1LE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA0LE_0LC1LC_1LE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head sweeps the whole tape. Its background is 0111 (after a sweep to the right) or the period-8 word 01001111 (after a sweep to the left), and the sweeps over it in both directions are proved shift rules. A handful of short defects split the background into long domains, and how the defects move and grow has not been made into a rule. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide, and proves the shift rules of the sweeps (lean/Rules.lean); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: D with 1 two left, 1 left, 0 under the head. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 32,248 cells have been visited and 21,407 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.288).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: The sweeps over the background: rightward L B> (01001111)^n R and L 1 C> (10011110)^n R (the left-sweep form becomes (0111)^2 per copy), leftward L (11010011)^n D>1 R and L (10100111)^n C>0 R (back to the period-8 form), for every n and all tapes L, R.

claims.title: A few long domains
claims.text: At step 394,721,780 (width 19,836) the tape is (1110)^3460, (0111)^200, (0111)^1206, (0111)^74 and short defects such as 1^8 0 1^3 0 1^6 or 1^17; at step 1,484,459,896 (width 39,113) the domains are 1676, 6498, 10, 552, 1018 copies long. The number of defects stays small (four to six); their motion was not reduced to a rule.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 22, history 1 up to width 22, history 2 up to width 20, history 3 up to width 18, LRU history up to width 3 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 16, p = 3 up to width 16, p = 4 up to width 16, p = 6 up to width 16. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..7; n = 8 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts on F1, reached as 1 A>1 (A reads 1, moves left onto a 1). The sweeps over the background never produce it; a halt would have to come from a defect, and the defects have no known rule.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is the four cells 0111 repeated, in long stretches separated by a few short defects. The head crosses the stretches by proved rules, but the defects change in a way nobody has pinned down.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 32,248 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
Short defects between long domains of 0111, at every sweep seen.

sections.heading: One background, two forms
html: After a sweep to the right the tape repeats 0111; a sweep to the left turns each pair 01110111 into 01001111, and the next rightward sweep turns it back. The four shift rules of these sweeps are proved (lean/Rules.lean). Two consecutive end turns:
Each domain of (0111)^2m is a domain of (01001111)^m on the way back.

sections.heading: A few defects between long domains
html: The domains are separated by short words such as 1^8 0 1^3 0 1^6 or 1^17. There are only four to six of them, and the domains between them are long and uneven: 3460, 200, 1206, 74 copies at step 3.9·108; 1676, 6498, 10, 552, 1018 at step 1.5·109. At the left end a block 1^N grows by about one cell per sweep while the domain next to it shrinks. The defects move from sweep to sweep, and their rule has not been worked out.

sections.heading: One pattern at a defect
html: F1 is the only halting transition, reached as 1 A>1. Inside a domain the sweeps never do that, so a halt would have to happen at a defect or an end. That question is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.288).
After 109 steps the tape spans 32,248 cells (22,435 left of the start, 987 right), with a density of 1s of 0.664.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A bouncer over the background 0111, written (0111)^2 after a sweep to the right and 01001111 after a sweep to the left; the tape is a few long domains of it separated by short defects, which drift and change length from sweep to sweep with no known rule.
family: period-4/8 bouncer with a few drifting defects
